topic.description: a subject in the knowledge graph. Any entity may be one by wearing this: a subject of its own is topic + doc + content, and a project is its own topic, so what is known about it sits under it. Its doc is the cover: the title, and a line or two saying what belongs under it. Its content.body is the contents: what is understood about it, written as one document citing its sources. Its edges say what it holds (contains: a subtopic, or anything else, such as a memory, a design, a skill, a package or somebody's words), what to understand first (requires), what it reads or references, and what it cites; beliefs are about it (belief.about)

name.description: the title in lowercase, its spaces single; no two topics share one, so a name said again finds the topic that has it. A name, not an identity: it changes with the title, and the entity keeps its eid

scope.description: the project it holds for; absent for a topic that holds everywhere, as world or fleet knowledge

tends.description: the relation on a link from a persona to the topic it looks after, its oracle: it keeps the topic's cover, contents and edges true and answers what is asked about it. It puts nothing in the persona's context; what the persona contains does

topic_new.title: Make a topic
topic_new.description: Make a topic, where no existing topic fits; a project is already its own topic. name is what it is called, as plain and general as the subject is ("testing", "ui components", "naming"), never a phrase about one point; body is its cover, a line or two saying what belongs under it, never a point anybody made. scope names the project it holds for; leave it out for a topic that holds everywhere. One name is one topic: a name that is taken is refused with the topic that has it, to use instead, and so is a name whose words hold another topic's or are held by them ("economic market design" beside "market design"). Returns the applied bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components); the topic's id is its entity.eid.

name.description: what the topic is called, a few plain words

body.description: a line or two saying what belongs under it

scope.description: project id or name it holds for; omit for a topic that holds everywhere

topic_find.title: Find topics
topic_find.description: Find existing topics: those whose name, title or cover holds each word in said, as the start of a word or by its stem ("data modeling" finds "data model", "tests" finds "testing"), ranked by meaning to the entity near names when the server has a vector index, or, given neither, the topics in order of name. Use it to find what is known about a subject (graph_show on a topic lists what it holds), before putting something you wrote under its topic (topic_add), and before making a topic, with near set to what you are filing under one, so a subject already named is reused rather than named again in other words. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components), each whole; limit defaults to 12.

said.description: words the topic's name, title or cover holds, as the start of a word or by its stem

near.description: an entity id or name whose meaning ranks the topics

topic_add.title: Add to a topic
topic_add.description: Put entities under a topic, where whoever reads the topic finds them: a memory, a design, a skill, a package, somebody's words, or a subtopic. Each gets a contains edge from the topic; adding one already there changes nothing, and drop takes them out instead. One entity may sit under several topics. Find the topic first with topic_find, or make one with topic_new; a project is its own topic, so its id or name places things under it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

topic.description: the topic's id or title, or a project's

ids.description: the entities to put under it, by id

drop.description: take them out of the topic instead
